LHX.sentence: L3Harris has fallen more than a quarter from its high, which is unusually steep for a steady defense contractor, but nothing has really changed — military spending keeps flowing their way.

ASML.sentence: ASML dropped about 7% in a single day, which looks dramatic, but they're still the only company on earth that makes the machines needed to print the most advanced chips — so this is a wobble in the stock, not a crack in the business.

LIN.sentence: Linde had a quiet, slightly up week — they supply oxygen, nitrogen and other industrial gases on long contracts and nudge prices up a little each quarter, which is the whole story with this one.

MSFT.sentence: Microsoft slipped slightly today but has quietly outpaced its peers over the past month — the Azure-cloud-and-AI story just keeps grinding along without much drama.

TMO.sentence: Thermo Fisher drifted down a touch as lab and biotech spending sits near a low point in its cycle — demand is soft for now, but they're still the go-to supplier of the equipment every research lab needs.

CVX.sentence: Chevron ticked up with oil prices, which are running high because fighting involving Iran has disrupted Persian Gulf shipments — so these fat profits are coming from the oil price, not from anything Chevron itself did.

NOW.sentence: ServiceNow has fallen sharply — down nearly half from its high — which is a big move for such a steady software company, even as corporations keep signing on for its workflow-automation and AI tools.

GLNCY.sentence: Glencore held up better than copper prices this week because its giant commodity-trading arm cushions the blow when any one metal weakens.

MLM.sentence: Martin Marietta is flat, and while its reported selling price looks like it dipped, that's just a mix of what sold — the actual price it gets per ton of crushed stone is still creeping up, which is what matters for this quarry business.

KOF.sentence: Coca-Cola FEMSA was quiet, though a weaker Mexican peso is the main thing tugging on its value since most of its sales are in pesos.

UBER.sentence: Uber slipped a touch, but people keep booking a lot more rides and food orders than before, and the real question hanging over it is whether self-driving car companies choose to run on its app or go it alone.

AMKBY.sentence: Maersk, the Danish container-shipping giant, is quiet, and it's trading for less than the value of its own fleet of ships — a sign the market isn't expecting much from global trade right now.

MA.sentence: Mastercard is basically flat, and people keep tapping their cards more than ever, so there's no real news here beyond the usual steady toll-collecting business.

ISRG.sentence: The da Vinci surgical-robot maker fell nearly 3% and is well off its high, yet hospitals keep doing more procedures on its machines and it's still outrunning its medical-device peers — a case of fear outrunning the facts.
